newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson taking $134 million charge to close stores.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson taking $134 million charge to close stores.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp. said Friday it will take a pre-tax charge of $134 million in the fourth quarter to close a number of stores, including 10 underperforming stores in its Mervyn's chain.
Dayton Hudson, which currently operates 1,101 stores in 38 states under three names, also said it was selling all its 25 Mervyn's stores in Georgia and Florida.

"Given Mervyn's limited market penetration in Florida and Georgia, it became clear that the best course of action was to exit these markets," Chairman and Chief Executive Bob Ulrich said in a statement.
The Minneapolis-based retailer said the $134 million charge, equal to about 35 cents a share, would cover the writedown of real estate assets and store closing costs.
The charge will also cover the previously announced closure of a Marshall Field's store in Park Forest, Ill., and the renovation of Marshall Field's downtown Milwaukee store.
The company said it did not anticipate any employees losing their jobs as a result of the announced actions.
It said that as a result of the real estate transactions, it expects to generate about $350 million in cash, which will be used to reduce debt and pursue growth opportunities.
It added that the net impact of the actions involving its Mervyn's unit will be to reduce annual revenue by about $375 million, based on 1996 performance.

"Our three retail divisions are core to Dayton Hudson's overall corporate strategy," Ulrich said. "We remain committed to ... improving the performance of the corporation and believe that this real estate repositioning will help us strengthen our competitive position and achieve our long-term financial goals."
Dayton Hudson said Dillard Department Stores Inc. agreed to buy 10 of 18 Mervyn's locations in Florida and JCPenney agreed to purchase three of seven Georgia locations.
The remaining properties are expected to be sold to a variety of other purchasers, it added.
Dayton Hudson also said it will sell or close about 10 poor-performing Mervyn's stores throughout the chain over the next 12 to 18 months.
In addition to 65 Dayton Hudson department stores, the company also operates 300 Mervyn's stores and 736 Target stores.
Dayton Hudson's stock gained $1.125 to $38 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
